privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how enpii studio (“we”) collects, uses, and protects information when you use EnStorage (the “Service”). EnStorage is a self-hosted application: all data is processed on an instance you control, and your files are stored directly in your own Google Drive account. By using the Service, you agree to the practices described below.
privacy.dataWeCollectBody:
Basic Google profile: When you sign in or connect an account with Google, we receive your name, email address, and profile picture (OIDC scopes `userinfo.profile` and `userinfo.email`). We use this to identify your account and personalize the interface.

OAuth tokens: For each Google Drive account you connect, we store an access token, a refresh token, and its expiry. Refresh tokens are encrypted with AES-256 at rest before being written to the database. We never receive or see your Google password.

File metadata: We store the metadata required to manage files (name, size, MIME type, folder path, upload date, star flags, share link token and settings, and the object ID in Google Drive). The file itself lives in your Google Drive account, not on our server.

API keys & webhooks: When you create a personal access token, only a bcrypt hash and the 8-character prefix are stored. The plaintext token is shown once and cannot be retrieved again. For webhooks we store the label, target URL, event list, and an encrypted secret.

Usage data: We log basic request metadata (timestamp, endpoint, status code, API key ID) for security, auditing of sensitive actions, and abuse prevention. We do not ship third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking pixels.
privacy.howWeUseBody:
We use the information collected solely to operate the Service as you request: authenticating you, routing file writes to the Google Drive account with the largest remaining quota, storing and retrieving your files, generating the share links you ask for, showing combined quota totals, and notifying you of account activity through webhooks.

We do not sell, rent, trade, or relinquish your personal information to third parties. We do not use your Google Drive data — including its content, names, or any metadata — for unrelated tracking, targeted advertising, or training general-purpose artificial intelligence / machine learning models.
privacy.googleScopes: 3. Google Drive API Policy & OAuth2 Scopes
privacy.googleScopesBody:
EnStorage connects to Google Drive on your behalf, and therefore must comply with the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

The scopes we request are limited to the file-management functionality you explicitly ask for:

- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` — create, read, update, and delete files and folders created by EnStorage inside the `EnStorage` folder on your Drive.
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly` — list and read file metadata, and read account quota information (`about.get`) when you enable quota monitoring and cross-cloud sync.
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile` and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email` — basic profile for sign-in.

All of these are non-default scopes and are only requested on the Google consent screen after you press the connect or sign-in button. We never access files outside the structure you manage through EnStorage, never share credentials or tokens with third parties, and never request access to Google services other than Drive and the basic profile.

Transparency note: in some configurations (for example scanning an existing folder structure or reading an account's global quota), your instance may request a broader Drive scope. Consent is always displayed explicitly by Google on the consent screen, and you are free to revoke it at any time.
privacy.limitedUseBody:
In line with the Limited Use principles of the Google API Services User Data Policy, we state that:

- We only use or share user data accessed from Google APIs to provide or allow access to legitimate EnStorage features that are relevant to you.
- We never sell Google Drive user data in any way.
- We never use or share that data for advertising, regardless of its source.
- We never use or allow the use of that data to train machine learning or AI models, including generative AI models, either directly or as part of another project or product.
- We restrict access to that data only to personnel who need it to process it on our behalf, and ensure they are bound by confidentiality obligations.

Self-hosted instances run on your own infrastructure, so the data controller for your Google Drive data is you, not enpii studio.
privacy.sharingBody:
Files or folders you choose to share can be accessed by anyone holding the share link. Links contain a random token and can be given an expiry date and a maximum view count. Links can be revoked at any time from the Folder or File page, or through the REST API (`DELETE /api/v1/files/{id}/share`).

When a folder is shared, its files are rendered through the EnStorage proxy so your private Google Drive links are never exposed to the recipient. You remain responsible for the content you share through those links.
privacy.thirdPartyBody:
We rely on the following third parties to operate the Service:

Google (OAuth2 & Google Drive API): processing is subject to the Google Privacy Policy. We only request the scopes needed to handle sign-in and the file management you ask for, in accordance with the Limited Use clause above.

Hosting infrastructure: on self-hosted instances all data resides on servers you control. On managed deployments, data may transit the infrastructure used to run the Service.

Email providers: if your instance sends transactional email (for example notifications or password resets), mail is routed through the SMTP configuration you provide.
privacy.securityBody:
We apply industry-standard measures to protect your data:

- Transport: all web, mobile, and REST API communication is served over HTTPS/TLS.
- OAuth tokens: access and refresh tokens are encrypted with AES-256 at rest in your self-hosted local database, with the key derived from your instance's `APP_KEY`.
- API keys: stored as a bcrypt hash plus a plaintext prefix for lookup; the secret value can never be read back.
- Account passwords: hashed one-way, never stored in plaintext.
- Isolation: files, folders, and Drive credentials are scoped per user so other users cannot read them.
- Rate limiting and audit logs for sensitive actions.

Full details of the security architecture are on the Security & Google API Disclosure page. No system is completely secure; if you discover a vulnerability, follow the reporting procedure described on that page.
privacy.retentionBody:
Your files remain in your Google Drive account until you delete them. Deleting a file or folder moves it to a soft-deleted state and it is permanently removed after 30 days unless you restore it.

Specific deletions:

- Detaching a Google account: when you revoke a Google account from EnStorage, we attempt to revoke the token at Google, then permanently delete the refresh token, access token, and all file metadata associated with that account from the database.
- Deleting your EnStorage account: all of your rows (files, folders, share links, API keys, webhooks, activity logs, and Google tokens) are permanently deleted through cascade relations, and tokens are revoked at Google. Files that remain in your Drive are still yours and you can manage them directly in Drive.
- Share links: revocation takes effect immediately; expired tokens are revoked automatically by a scheduler.

Once access is revoked, EnStorage has no way to read the contents of your Drive anymore.
privacy.yourRightsBody:
You hold full control over access to your data:

- Revoking access: remove the Google account from the Google Accounts page in EnStorage, or open Google Account Settings → Security → Third-party apps & services (myaccount.google.com/permissions) and revoke EnStorage. Revoking on Google's side also severs the connection permanently.
- Deleting data: delete files, folders, or share links at any time; delete your account from the Profile page to erase all local metadata.
- Portability: every operation is available through the REST API, so you can export your file listing and contents programmatically.
- Access & correction: review or change your profile, language, and password from the Profile page.

If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or California, you have additional rights under applicable law (GDPR / CCPA), including the right to data portability and the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. On self-hosted deployments you exercise these requests through your instance administrator.
privacy.changesBody: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Material changes will be announced through the Service and on this page together with the “Last updated” date. Continued use of the Service after changes indicates acceptance of the updated policy.
privacy.contactBody: For privacy questions, questions about Google API Services User Data Policy compliance, or to exercise your rights, contact us at enpiiofficial@gmail.com. For security issues, use the vulnerability reporting channel on the Security page.

security.title: Security & Google API Disclosure
security.intro: This page describes EnStorage's security architecture and our formal disclosure regarding use of the Google Drive API. It applies to every client: web, mobile, and REST API. The guiding principle is simple — EnStorage is never the storage. Your files stay in your Google Drive account while our system manages only tokens, routing, and metadata on the instance you control.
security.architectureBody:
When you upload a file, the backend receives the byte stream from your client and forwards it directly (multipart / resumable upload) to the destination Google Drive account inside the `EnStorage` folder. The instance does not write files to disk as permanent storage and keeps no copy warehouse.

As a result:

- No third-party server ever holds the contents of your files.
- Revoking access immediately stops the system's ability to read your Drive.
- Detaching an account or deleting the instance leaves no hidden copy with us, because we never had one.
security.transportBody: Every data path runs over HTTPS/TLS: web pages, the mobile app, OAuth callbacks, the stream/preview proxy, and all REST API endpoints. We recommend serving public deployments behind a reverse proxy with valid certificates, HSTS, and regularly updated TLS suites. Security headers are sent on web responses, and shared content is rendered through the proxy so your Google Drive object IDs are never leaked to end clients.
security.atRest: 3. Encryption at Rest for OAuth Tokens
security.atRestBody:
Google access and refresh tokens are stored encrypted with AES-256 at rest in the local database (`AES-256-CBC` cipher), with the encryption key derived from your instance's `APP_KEY`, which is never stored alongside the database.

Operational consequences you should understand:

- If the `APP_KEY` is lost, stored tokens cannot be recovered and every Google account must be reconnected.
- Because that key is yours, we are cryptographically unable to open your tokens.
- We recommend volume encryption on the database host, encrypted backups, and planned `APP_KEY` rotation in line with your organization's security policy.
security.credentialsBody:
Account passwords are one-way hashed with bcrypt and are never stored or transmitted in plaintext. API keys are generated in the format `en_<8-char-prefix>_<40-char-secret>`; only the bcrypt hash and the prefix are stored in the database, while the secret value is displayed once at creation and cannot be retrieved afterwards. Inbound requests are verified by matching the prefix and then comparing the hash (bcrypt compare).

In addition: every request is logged with its key ID, scopes are enforced per endpoint (`read`, `write`, `delete`, `full`), keys can expire or be revoked at any time, and rate limiting thwarts brute-force attempts. We recommend one key per integration with the minimum scope, plus periodic rotation.
security.scopesBody:
EnStorage only requests the Google scopes needed for the features you enable, and never silently: `drive.file` for file management inside app-created folders, `drive.readonly` for file listing and quota reads, and `userinfo.profile` / `userinfo.email` for the basic sign-in profile. The Google consent screen explicitly shows the requested scopes before any token is issued, and consent is granted by you, not by us.

Refresh tokens are used only to reissue access tokens for operations on your account's behalf; we never sell, share, or publish Google credentials to third parties. The app is designed to meet the verification requirements and the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
security.limitedUseBody:
We comply with the Limited Use requirements of the Google API Services User Data Policy. We explicitly state that Google Drive user data:

- Is never sold or rented to anyone.
- Is never used for advertising or unrelated tracking beyond the features you request.
- Is never used to train general-purpose machine learning or artificial intelligence models, by us or by anyone acting on our behalf.
- Is never shared with third parties except for processing on our behalf under confidentiality obligations, or where lawfully required.
- Is only accessed as strictly necessary to perform the file-management functions you instruct.
security.isolationBody: Every database row — files, folders, Google accounts, API keys, share links, and activity logs — is scoped to its owner's `user_id` and verified on each request. User A's Google accounts cannot be seen, referenced, or used to store User B's files. `owner` and `member` roles differ only in governance actions (user invitations and system-wide audit logs) and never grant access to another user's Drive credentials. API key and Google account management endpoints accept user sessions only and reject API key authentication.
security.sharingBody: Share links use unguessable random tokens, can be given an expiry date and a maximum view count, and can be revoked instantly from the UI or the API. Shared files and folders are rendered through a proxy so the original Google Drive URL is never exposed. Links that expire or reach their view limit are revoked automatically by a scheduler. We recommend always setting an expiry and a view limit when sharing sensitive content.
security.loggingBody: The instance records request metadata (timestamp, endpoint, status code, key/session identity) and audit logs for sensitive actions such as API key creation/revocation, Google account connection/revocation, share link changes, and delete operations. These logs serve security and forensic needs, not behavioral profiling. No third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking pixels ship in the codebase. Because the instance is yours, log retention and access are under your administrator's control.
security.userControlsBody:
You can revoke access at any time through two independent paths:

- From EnStorage: open the Google Accounts page and choose Revoke. The system revokes the token at Google (best effort) and permanently deletes the refresh token, access token, and related metadata from the database.
- From Google: open myaccount.google.com/permissions, select EnStorage, and revoke access. You can also review and sign out of sessions via myaccount.google.com/signin.

After revocation the tokens are worthless and the system can no longer read or write files in your Drive. Deleting your EnStorage account from the Profile page performs a thorough deletion of all your local metadata plus token revocation at Google.
security.deletion: 11. Data Deletion & Right to Be Forgotten
security.deletionBody: Deletion is permanent and layered: detaching a Google account removes that account's tokens and related metadata; deleting your EnStorage account removes files, folders, share links, API keys, webhooks, logs, and tokens through cascade relations; shutting down the instance removes all metadata from your system. Files in your Google Drive can be deleted directly from Drive, and the cleanup scheduler reconciles that state on the metadata side. Since file contents never reside on our servers, no additional deletion request to enpii studio is needed.
security.userResponsibilitiesBody:
Because EnStorage is self-hosted, the security of your deployment is also your responsibility. We recommend:

- Keeping `APP_KEY` in a secret manager, never in the database or a repository.
- Restricting database access and accepting connections only from the application network.
- Serving the instance behind a reverse proxy with current TLS, HSTS, and rate limiting.
- Applying security updates regularly and keeping encrypted database backups.
- Enabling two-step verification on connected Google accounts and creating minimum-scope API keys.
- Removing unused accounts, revoking unused API keys, and reviewing activity logs periodically.
security.vulnerabilityBody:
If you find a vulnerability in EnStorage, please report it responsibly to enpiiofficial@gmail.com with the subject “Security”. Do not publish vulnerability details (public issues, social media, or blog posts) before it is addressed.

Upon receiving a report we will acknowledge it within at most 7 days, assess impact and severity, prepare a fix or mitigation for the next release, and coordinate a disclosure timeline with you if you would like credit. Please avoid accessing other users' production data, disrupting the service, or downloading data as evidence — demonstrating the vulnerable point is enough.
security.statusBody: No system is completely secure. Encryption protects tokens and transport, but it does not eliminate risks such as compromised Google credentials, misconfigured instances, or social engineering. We update this page as security practices evolve; material changes are announced through releases along with the “Last updated” date on this page. For the privacy aspects of your personal data see the Privacy Policy; for usage conditions see the Terms of Service.
